text:
One week on, here's the impact GTA 6's launch had on the industry so far

GTA 6 has been on sale for a week, and remained the dominant game and talking point across the games industry – supported, admittedly, by a quiet news week in America due to the Thanksgiving holiday. Beyond its record-breaking day-one revenue haul, it's now possible to start judging its impact on the wider industry, and consider if the anticipation – and in some cases, anxiety – was justified.

author: GamesIndustry.biz
text:
GTA 6's pirate PC ports: new tools, old problem | Opinion

I'm sorry in advance. I know we'd all far prefer to be spending our time running around the sun-soaked dystopia of Vice City this week rather than spending it reading yet another column about the game, but we need to talk about GTA 6 again. Specifically, we need to talk about the side story that's spun off from the game's launch – namely the scramble to get it running on PC, before Rockstar itself has so much as officially announced a PC version. It's a story that's getting an outsized amount of attention precisely because GTA 6 is involved, but the consequences of what's playing out will reach far beyond Rockstar or Take-Two.

Indie puzzle adventure Rhell beats GTA 6 to win Best Game Made in The North at the Game Republic Awards

At the Game Republic Awards in Wakefield last night, the indie puzzle adventure Rhell: Warped Worlds and Troubled Times beat off competition from the likes of Grand Theft Auto 6, Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, and Wardogs to take home the prize for Best Game Made in The North.
